title: GraphQL APIs
description: Production GraphQL reference covering schemas, types, nullability, operations, variables, fragments, directives, resolvers, execution, DataLoader, pagination, mutations, subscriptions, caching, authorization, query limits, federation, testing, observability, and evolution.

subtopics.title: Object Types, Fields & Nullability
subtopics.description: The schema is a typed capability graph. Make nullability reflect real guarantees because a non-null field failure propagates to the nearest nullable parent.

callouts.title: Non-Null Is an Availability Promise
callouts.text: Do not mark fields non-null merely because clients prefer them. A downstream failure can null a larger response subtree when the guarantee is broken.

subtopics.title: Interfaces, Unions, Enums & Input Objects
subtopics.description: Interfaces share fields across implementing types, unions model alternatives without shared fields, enums constrain symbolic values, and input objects model structured arguments.

callouts.title: Inputs and Outputs Are Separate Types
callouts.text: GraphQL object types cannot be reused as input objects. Design input contracts for commands and filters rather than mirroring database records.

subtopics.title: Domain Boundaries & Schema Evolution
subtopics.description: Name fields in domain language, expose stable capabilities rather than storage, add changes compatibly, deprecate with reasons, and measure usage before removal.

callouts.title: Version Fields, Not the Entire Endpoint, by Default
callouts.text: Add nullable fields, arguments with defaults, and new types compatibly. Breaking nullability, enum, argument, or semantic changes still require migration and usage evidence.

subtopics.title: Queries, Variables, Aliases & Fragments
subtopics.description: Name operations, pass values through variables, reuse fragments around UI/domain boundaries, and use aliases for multiple field selections with different arguments.

callouts.title: Variables Are Not String Interpolation
callouts.text: Send a static operation document plus separately encoded variables. Servers validate variable types and avoid query injection caused by building GraphQL source from user input.

subtopics.title: Resolvers, Execution & Errors
subtopics.description: Execution resolves selected fields, often concurrently by level. A resolver returns a value, promise, or error; errors include paths and can coexist with partial data.

callouts.title: Context Must Be Request-Scoped
callouts.text: Put authenticated identity, loaders, deadlines, and services in per-request context. Never share user-specific loaders or authorization decisions globally.

subtopics.title: Batching, DataLoader & N+1 Prevention
subtopics.description: Field-oriented execution can issue one query per parent. Request-scoped loaders batch keys and cache results while preserving input ordering and per-key errors.

callouts.title: Loader Keys Include Authorization Scope
callouts.text: Do not cache only by object ID when visibility differs by tenant, locale, role, or policy. Scope loaders per request and design keys around every factor affecting the result.

subtopics.title: Cursor Pagination & Connections
subtopics.description: Opaque stable cursors handle changing datasets better than offsets when ordering is deterministic. Return page information and apply bounded limits.

callouts.title: Cursor Encodes Position, Not Authorization
callouts.text: Treat cursors as untrusted opaque input, validate them, reapply filters and authorization, and use a unique deterministic tie-breaker in ordering.

subtopics.title: Mutations, Payloads & Idempotency
subtopics.description: Use verb-oriented mutation fields with explicit inputs and payloads. Validate and authorize inside the transaction boundary and support idempotency for retried external effects.

callouts.title: Top-Level Mutation Fields Execute Serially, Nested Work May Not
callouts.text: Do not rely on GraphQL execution alone for database atomicity. Define transactions, outbox/events, retry behavior, and partial external failure explicitly.

subtopics.title: Subscriptions & Incremental Delivery
subtopics.description: Subscriptions establish a long-lived event stream; incremental delivery can defer or stream selected response parts where implementation support exists. Both require lifecycle and backpressure design.

callouts.title: Reconnect Requires State Reconciliation
callouts.text: Events may be missed, duplicated, or reordered across disconnects. Define authorization rechecks, resume/catch-up behavior, heartbeats, limits, and cleanup.

subtopics.title: Authorization & Query Cost Controls
subtopics.description: Authenticate before execution and authorize every field/resource access. Bound document size, depth, aliases, list arguments, complexity, execution time, and result size.

codeBlocks.code:
Pre-parse: body/document bytes, operation count
Validate: known operation, depth, aliases, field/argument cost
Execute: deadline, cancellation, bounded loaders and downstream calls
Authorize: action + object + tenant at resolver/service boundary
Respond: bounded lists and stable redacted errors

callouts.title: Introspection Is Not the Primary Security Boundary
callouts.text: Disabling introspection does not replace authentication, authorization, limits, rate controls, or schema-safe errors. Assume attackers can discover capabilities.

subtopics.title: HTTP, Caching & Trusted Documents
subtopics.description: GraphQL commonly uses POST; safe query operations may use GET under an explicit policy. Cache normalized entities or persisted operation responses with identity and variable scope.

callouts.title: Cache Keys Include Authorization Context
callouts.text: A document hash and variables are insufficient when results depend on caller, tenant, locale, feature flags, or policy. Prevent private results entering shared caches.

subtopics.title: Federation, Testing & Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Federated graphs need clear entity ownership, composition checks, compatible rollout, routing health, and cross-subgraph authorization and observability.

codeBlocks.code:
Schema: lint + breaking/dangerous change checks + operation registry
Resolvers: unit policy/mapping + integration datastore tests
Operations: client contract and persisted-document tests
Performance: representative complexity, N+1 and loader batch metrics
Telemetry: operation name/hash, resolver errors, downstream spans, no raw variables

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: Model nullability honestly, evolve compatibly, scope loaders per request, bound pagination and query cost, authorize every resource, redact errors/variables, monitor resolver/downstream latency, test schema composition, and rehearse partial dependency failure.
